title: Response Surface SLO Compass — model & endpoint p50/p95/p99 with I/O-mode layers
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Create a consolidated SLO-facing dashboard ("Response Surface SLO Compass") that surfaces p50/p95/p99 response times broken down by model family and API route with clear separation between streaming and non-streaming IO modes. The goal is a single-pane view product and infra SREs can use to triage regressions, validate rollouts, and communicate SLO posture to customers and sales. This ticket covers telemetry collection changes, trace hook instrumentation, histogram bucketing strategy, and dashboard panels + drilldowns.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 by model family and by route for last 1h/24h/7d with annotations for deploys and config changes
Panels include a toggle to split by IO mode (streaming vs non-streaming) and to overlay historical baseline visually
All latency numbers are derived from 100ms-resolution histogram aggregates emitted from runtime (no sampling bias) for the last 30 days
Trace links available from P95 and P99 rows that open flamegraph view scoped to the offending request shape
Alerting rules created for SLO breaches at p95 > threshold and p99 > threshold with runbook links
Dashboard performance: panels load within 2s for single model-family queries and under 6s for full-surface queries
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — aligned on scope with PM and SRE. Decided to reuse existing histogram metric prefix redwood.latency.hist_ms and add label io_mode and model_family.
2026-03-04: Runtime change merged to emit io_mode tag and request_shape in trace context (PR #428 welcome). Performance microbench run shows ~0.8% p99 overhead on heavy tails.

2026-03-07: Prototype dashboard wired in Grafana using histogram_quantile over histogram buckets. Early feedback: heavy cardinality from request_shape — agreed to roll up to route_name for the SLO compass.
2026-03-10: UX review with PM & Design — added explicit streaming toggle and baseline overlay. Design requested clearer error-rate inset per panel.
2026-03-12: Implemented trace link joiners in trace-service; P95 rows now link to traces filtered by model_family+route+io_mode. WIP: generating canary annotation events for deploy pipeline.
2026-03-14: Dashboard first pass in staging. Load test indicates full-surface queries take 5.7s. Filing follow-up ENG-582902 to optimize query materialization for cross-model rolls-ups.
comments: Mateo Alvarez: We should be careful with histogram bucket boundaries for long-tail models (LLMs produce heavy tails). Suggest exponential buckets starting at 1ms up to 60s with tighter density between 10ms-2s.
Asha Kapoor: Agreed. Also propose we compute p50/p95/p99 in the metrics pipeline (ingest sidecar) to avoid expensive ad-hoc histogram_quantile across high cardinality in Grafana.
Elena Park (SRE): Add deploy annotations from CI — having those clearly visible was key during last outage. Also add a per-route error-rate inset so we can correlate latency vs errors.
PM: Include a short 'how to use' panel for support and sales, describing which panels to check first for a customer-facing incident.
technical_notes: Instrumentation: add io_mode and model_family labels at ingress; emit redwood.latency.hist_ms histogram with exponential buckets. Tracing hooks: propagate request_shape and model_variant tags; create trace link token in metrics pipeline. Aggregation: materialize p50/p95/p99 in metrics pipeline for low-cardinality rollups (model_family+route+io_mode) and retain raw histograms for on-demand deep dives. Querying: Grafana panels use materialized metrics for surface, histogram_quantile over raw histograms behind drilldowns. Rollouts: gated behind canary for 48h. Observe performance impact; if >1% CPU cost, fallback to sampling policy.
